text.p: Copper prices remained well below early highs during Monday afternoon LME trading, with the market ending an ultimately disappointing session virtually unchanged.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau was 0.72 points lower at 244.07.

LME copper traders said there was a lack of followthrough when prices reached a peak of $2,390 a tonne, with volumes thinning out, and the market subsequently settled back below the $2,380 chart level. "It ran up on the talk of Chinese buying, but they are more likely to be sellers at the highs. They want the price lower for the really big buying they have to do," one trader said. Three months prices finished the kerb at $2,367 a tonne, down just $1 from Friday's kerb close. The cash/threes backwardation was at $55/60.
Elsewhere, action and price movements were dictated by copper, with early firmness fading across the board.
Aluminium backtracked from a test of $1,670 and closed the session at $1,657, unchanged from Friday. Nickel slumped away from above $7,900 and was $135 lower at $7,820 at the end of the kerb.
Lead and zinc both moved in tamdem, with the former metal suffering from a late sell-off to close at $679, down $13. Zinc slipped under $1,300 again, and was $3 softer at $1,294.
Tin continued to weaken, with stocks seen rising once more, and prices ended at $5,870, down $55. Alloy was quoted at $1,545/550.

CBOT wheat futures were slightly lower at midsession, weakened mainly by spillover selling from corn and soybean pits, traders said. Dealers noted news that Egypt had bought 150,000 tonnes of wheat. The total included 100,000 tonnes from Australia and 50,000 tonnes from either Australia or the U.S. Bearish sentiment on charts also weighed on the market. "We did a lot of damage to the charts Friday," one dealer commented. At 1125 CST May wheat was off 3-1/2 cents a bushel at $3.86-1/2 per bushel with other months off 2-3/4 to 1-1/2 cents.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures remained sharply lower in early afternoon trading, but silver bucked the trend by rebounding and moving higher. A floor source said silver had initially dipped to a low of $5.12 in the May contract, hitting a double bottom and moved back up after a trade house come in to buy. At 1311 EST COMEX April gold was down $2.60 at $350.90 an ounce, traded $351.60 to $349.40. COMEX May silver was up 2.0 cents at $5.185 an ounce, traded $5.21 to $5.12.

NYMEX crude oil prices were hanging heavy midday Monday amid talk of unsold Brent cargoes, dragging the refined products down as well, traders said. But product-to-crude crack spreads were holding up in the sell-off, keeping some of the bearish retracement going on in perspective, others said. "In spite of the fact we opened lower, the cracks are still doing well," said one floor trader. May crude, hurt by talk 10 Brent cargoes were hanging unsold in the Atlantic Basin, stood 21 cents lower at noon EST/1700 GMT at $21.30 a barrel.
